clue.text: Changes in it are due to inactivity

indicators.note: changes made to the words in it are tell us to reorder their letters

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone blames sluggishness for any alterations that happen to a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a synonym for sluggish inactivity, a tendency to stay still.

clue.text: Turn over at leisure

definitions.meaning: an engine left to turn over slowly without driving anything is said to be running this way

explanation.definitionFit: An engine ticking over is said to idle, and a person at leisure is idle, unoccupied.

clue.text: Regret raising old currency

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it from the bottom up, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to regret is to rue

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to see a former coinage brought back into circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' looks as if it describes the currency, but it only supplies O; RUE reversed gives EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the shared money of most European Union countries.

clue.text: Double-crosser, jailed more than once?

definitions.meaning: someone who betrays a partner, especially by being unfaithful
read playfully as a person who has served time twice

explanation.definitionFit: A cheating partner is called a two-timer, and someone who has done time twice could jokingly be one too.

clue.text: Accept a proposal in Gretna Green

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words of the place name that follow

explanation.surface: A couple say yes to marriage at Gretna Green, the Scottish village famed for runaway weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was where eloping English couples went to marry, which fits the proposal picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to say yes to, or accept, something that is proposed.

clue.text: Judge accepts story in mitigation

indicators.note: one thing accepting another takes it in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a referee, REF for short, judges a game
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A judge hears a tale offered to lessen a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture makes 'Judge' look like a magistrate, but it is the sports referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is easing or lessening of pain or hardship, a synonym for mitigation.

clue.text: Times' editor taken out

parts.note: times are periods or eras

explanation.surface: An editor at The Times newspaper has been removed from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times'' looks like the newspaper, but it simply means periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erased has been rubbed or deleted out, so it is taken out.

clue.text: It's no good to repeat things to the ignorant

parts.note: ill can mean bad or no good, as in ill fortune
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Telling things over and over is pointless to people who do not know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'things' are link words smoothing the surface; ILL then ITERATE make the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The illiterate, as a collective noun, are those unable to read, and so uneducated or ignorant.

clue.text: Tried if car crash results in a death, relatively speaking

indicators.note: a car crash smashes things up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A court asks whether a motor accident caused a fatality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively speaking' makes the definition a killing among relatives: specifically of a brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Fratricide is the killing of one's own brother, a death within the family.

clue.text: Left fat pig inside

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: Lard is left with a pig inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: LARBOARD is the old nautical word for the left-hand side of a ship, now called port.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the archaic sailors' term for port, the left side of a vessel facing forward.

clue.text: Pea soup everyone sent back — another dish wanted

indicators.note: a soup is a mixture, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, three letters to rearrange

indicators.note: something sent back is reversed, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A diner returns the pea soup and orders a different course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' looks like the dish, but it only stirs the letters of 'Pea' into PAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella, the Spanish rice dish, is another dish besides the soup.

clue.text: Make clear the river is stocked with fish

indicators.note: a river stocked with fish holds them, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A notice explains that the river has been filled with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to turn it into plain meaning, making it clear.

clue.text: It may reveal hidden charges

parts.note: charges here are explosive charges buried underground, not fees concealed on a bill

explanation.definitionFit: A mine detector is a device that finds buried explosive mines.

clue.text: Her cue kept being misplaced — a difficult position with no means of moving forward?

definitions.text: a difficult position with no means of moving forward?

indicators.note: letters being misplaced are put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A snooker player keeps losing her cue and so cannot play on.
explanation.walkthrough: The full idiom is 'up the creek without a paddle': stuck, with no way to move forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in trouble with no way out is the idiom's meaning, from being stranded on a creek without a paddle.

clue.text: Shorts designed for hill-climbing?

parts.note: read as clothing for one's seat, worn while walking uphill; really the lowest ratio a vehicle uses on a steep slope

explanation.definitionFit: Bottom gear is the lowest gear, used for climbing hills; shorts are also gear for one's bottom.

clue.text: Business statement

definitions.meaning: one's line of work or occupation
a declaration, as in a ... of faith

explanation.definitionFit: A profession is a trade or career, and also an open declaration of belief.

clue.text: Reason to speak about raising money

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the other

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it upwards, reversing it

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone has grounds to talk about fundraising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' looks like a verb or a cause, but it is the noun meaning a sound mind; 'raising' only applies to money, written upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind is a synonym for sanity.

clue.text: This fabulous bird reciprocates a surprised expression

indicators.note: to reciprocate is to give back, so the expression is turned back to front; the bird's letters also sit inside this word, a coincidence

parts.note: 'cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A legendary bird answers in kind when someone gasps in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian legend, so a fabulous one.

clue.text: Paul came out with an admission of guilt

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Paul emerged confessing what he had done.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul coming out also hints at confession; the Latin phrase means 'my fault'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa, Latin for my fault, is a confession that one is to blame.

clue.text: Capital investment

parts.note: capital read as the head, and investment as clothing put on; not money put into a business

explanation.definitionFit: A hat is something worn on the head, which is jokingly one's capital, so dressing it is an investment.

clue.text: Though concerned, possibly resented it

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone cares about a matter but may well have resented it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being interested in a matter means being concerned or involved in it.

clue.text: Attractive bar in which we first met Bunter

definitions.meaning: a bar of metal that draws iron to it

definitions.text: in which we first met Bunter
definitions.meaning: the British boys' story paper in which the fat schoolboy Billy Bunter first appeared

explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet attracts iron, and The Magnet was the comic weekly where Billy Bunter of Greyfriars School first appeared.

clue.text: Promise non-U field event records

parts.note: a compact is an agreement or promise

indicators.note: non-U tells us the letter U is left out of the word

parts.note: the discus is a field event in athletics

explanation.surface: An athlete promises to stay away from posh field events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is also old British slang for not upper class; here it just removes U from DISCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact discs are recordings of music, so they are records.

clue.text: "Not out" the umpire is upset to conclude

parts.note: a batsman not out in cricket is still in

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: an umpire is a referee, REF for short

explanation.surface: An umpire is unhappy to give a cricket batsman not out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out' is cricket: a batsman who is not out is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion from evidence, so to conclude.

clue.text: Army team transport

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a team in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A military squad needs vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a form of transport.

clue.text: I stole away to an isolated spot

indicators.note: away means the following word is taken out of the one before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: I crept off to a remote place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole away' reads as slipping off, but 'away' removes TO from STOLE to leave SLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a small island, a spot cut off by water.

clue.text: They walk out of the play

definitions.text: They walk out of the play

parts.words: They walk out of the play
parts.note: reads as theatregoers leaving in disgust; really the Latin stage direction for actors leaving the stage

explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the stage direction meaning that several actors leave the stage.

clue.text: Dumps substandard cargoes

parts.note: off means below standard, as food going off
loads are cargoes

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of poor-quality shipments.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload is to unload or get rid of something, so to dump it.

clue.text: Shrewish girl set about painter in unarmed combat

indicators.note: one piece is set about, or around, the other

parts.note: Kate is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered young woman attacked an artist with her bare hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' reads as attacked, but it is the container signal. RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of fighting without weapons.

clue.text: Understand that lies are wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that telling falsehoods is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or come to understand it.
